detail.longDescription: arXiv:2608.20137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern optimizing compilers rely on heuristic search algorithms for NP-hard optimization problems, which can result in poor generated-code performance and long or unpredictable compile times. These are considered bugs by users, but verified compilers rarely reason beyond semantic preservation. We propose verifying performance and compile time properties of compiler passes. As a proof-of-concept, we formulate inline expansion using a cost model estimating instruction-cache performance. We mechanize this in Rocq, prove semantic preservation of the inlining transformation, and verify the algorithm's monotone improvement, convergence-time bound, and performance bounds for intermediate and final solutions.
